MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 7, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:05 p.m., on January 7, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on December 20, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title “Council Member.”

Present:  Council Member Leckness
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  Council Member Ury

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Leckness

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that items CS1 and CS2 are no longer necessary because the
matters have been resolved in the City's favor. He recommended that those items be removed from
the agenda so the Council can concentrate on the personnel matters, items CS3 and CS4.

City Council Minutes  1  January 7, 2013
 CS3. Labor Negotiations -- The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations are the
  City and the City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator is Dennis
  Wilberg.

CS4. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:11 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Ury
was absent.)

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was no need for the City Council to address items
CS1 and CS2 as staff accomplished the Council's December 21, 2012, direction and these matters
were resolved in the City's favor.

Mr. Curley noted that the City Council discussed item CS3 and they deferred item CS4 to the next
meeting. There was no reportable action from Closed Session.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Opening Remarks from Mayor Reardon

  Mayor Reardon presented her goals for 2013.

P2. "Art Beat" Student Art Competition Awards

  Mayor Reardon presented awards to Monica Brazil, Madelaine Hsu, Annie Kwon, Rachel
  La Course, Jason Nimitjaroonhsu, Mosellé Royal, and Katharine Schultz.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Maurer, M.V.: announced that the Orange County School of the Arts and Timeless Melodies
will perform the music of Rodgers and Hammerstein in "Oh What a Beautiful Evening." The
concert will be held on January 31, 2013, at 7:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center.

Rob Frias, President of Mission Viejo Pony Baseball, M.V.: discussed the growth of Pony Baseball
City Council Minutes  2  January 7, 2013
 in town and he asked the City Council for assistance in finding a permanent home for the Pony
League in Mission Viejo.

Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.: notified the Council that Casta del Sol resident and City volunteer John
Kiely passed away. A memorial service will be held on Sunday, January 13, 2013, at the Elk's
Lodge at 1:30 p.m. In lieu of flowers, his wife has asked that donations be made to the Elks
Foundation.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: asked the City Council to consider changing campaign finance rules for the
City of Mission Viejo. She noted that one outside company gave a candidate $10,000 to try and
influence the votes in the last election. Mrs. Reavis also asked the Council to set up a responsible
budget and require the employees to pick up more of the CalPERS burden.

Barbara Wegner, M.V.: expressed her disappointment in the City's policy that prohibits a
homeowner from installing artificial turf and she asked the City Council to address the issue at a
Council Meeting.

Harry Lenczyk, M.V.: expressed concern with the Council's recent vote to approve a dog park. He
suggested that the dog park be located adjacent to the Marguerite Tennis Center instead.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: noted his support for Mrs. Reavis' recommendations on campaign
contribution limitations and retirement reform. He further discussed a recent Orange County
Register article regarding a State review of toll road finances. He asked why the Council Members
who sit on the Toll Road Agency Boards have not reported on the decline in toll revenues.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: discussed the school shooting in Connecticut and stated that it brings her
comfort to know that there are School Resource Officers in Mission Viejo schools. She reminded
residents that Sierra and Montanoso Recreation Centers are not as crowded as the commercial
gyms and she encouraged residents to check out the family oriented centers. Lastly, she recounted
her attendance at yesterday's Elks Club bingo event which helped to raise funds for the purchase
of a new police dog for Mission Viejo.

City Manager’s Report

17. Report on Recent Actions of the Successor Agency Oversight Board

  City Manager Wilberg presented the report.

City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Curley announced that Southern California Edison (SCE) and Pacific Gas & Electric
(PG&E) are looking at the San Onofre reactor decommissioning budget and appear to be indicating
City Council Minutes  9  January 7, 2013
 that current funds are inadequate for future reactor shut downs. Staff will be looking to the Council
for direction on the plan to charge rate-payers additional fees to supplement the decommissioning
budget. The utility companies may or may not hold public hearings on the matter and Mr. Curley
will be asking Council to address this at the next meeting.

City Attorney Curley reminded the Council that before they can address the Kaleidoscope signage
issue, they will be asked to consider the broader subject of signage at the next City Council
Meeting. The community will have several opportunities to express opinions on signage prior to
Council deliberations on any Kaleidoscope proposal.

Mr. Curley answered questions of the City Council on the San Onofre matter and Council Member
Kelley requested that staff post information on the subject on the City's website as it becomes
available.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

18. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness thanked Mayor Reardon for recognizing the students who won awards
in the "Art Beat" competition earlier this evening. He noted that it is great to see the City
acknowledge creative work and he expressed his appreciation to staff for working to support the
arts.

Council Member Schlicht

Council member Schlicht thanked Ziggy Wilczynski for the floral arrangement that he gave her
before the meeting. She stated that she hoped everyone had a joyous Christmas season and she
wished a happy New Year to all. Council Member Schlicht noted that 2013 will be as good as we
make it and it will take hard work to get through these economically tough times. She outlined
her attendance at the recent NRC meeting in San Clemente regarding SCE's proposal to restart one
of the nuclear domes at San Onofre at 70% power. She expressed concern that SCE has not fixed
the problem and that rate payers may be asked to pay for SCE's mistakes. She also discussed her
attendance a CPUC public participation hearing regarding Smart Meters opt-out. Council Member
Schlicht stated that the power companies want residents to pay a fee to opt out and she feels that
this and the Smart Meters violate a person's constitutional rights. She further announced that there
are no opportunities for businesses to opt-out and they will be penalized for using extra
City Council Minutes  10  January 7, 2013
 electricity. Council Member Schlicht noted that there are a lot of issues surrounding these Smart
Meters and she plans to keep an eye on the situation. Lastly, she discussed the guest column that
she wrote on the City's financial health and she stated that she looks forward to very closely
examining the budget during the upcoming budget workshops. The City's finances will be her
main focus this year. Council Member Schlicht concluded with a quote from John Quincy Adams:
"Always stand on principal, even if you are alone."

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury was absent.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley thanked Ziggy Wilczynski for the rose and also for the wonderful display
he set up in the lobby of City hall. He has highlighted some of the history of Mission Viejo and
he places similar displays at the library every few weeks. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley noted that it
takes a lot of work and could only be done by someone who is a dedicated historian like Ziggy. She
also congratulated Barbara Dice who was named City Employee of the year for 2012 for going
above and beyond in her duties. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley touched on the tragic Connecticut school
shootings that recently shook the nation. She commended Mission Viejo Police Chief Chris
Wilson and the two school districts for proactively working on school safety. Mission Viejo has
five School Resource Officers and since the Connecticut incident, the officers and school officials
have been reviewing emergency plans and holding parent meetings to talk about the important
issue of school safety. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley thanked the City Council for being protective of
public safety and continuing to fund those School Resource officers. She also thanked the Mission
Viejo Activities Committee members for tirelessly helping in Santa's Workshop throughout
December and she noted that they do many wonderful things all year around. Those interested in
volunteering with the MVAC can contact her for more information. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
observed that the holidays are a time to focus on the blessing we enjoy in our lives and she
announced that she has been blessed with a new grandson who was born on December 8,
2012. She now has four grandchildren under the age of 4 and it was indeed a wonderful Christmas
and holiday season. Finally, Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that the Community of Character
word for the month of January is perseverance.
Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon thanked those who were present this evening and she thanked her colleagues for
their indulgence during her first meeting as Mayor. She outlined her attendance at recent events
including the staff holiday luncheon where Barbara Dice was recognized as the 2012 Employee of
the Year. Mrs. Dice helped to manage the financial side of the Improve Don't Move Program and
she noted that Barbara will be honored at a Council Meeting in February. Mayor Reardon also
commended the IT department for implementing a new software program at the library. The City
City Council Minutes  11  January 7, 2013
 has received accolades on the new features and she noted that the installation was seamless and
very transparent to the users of the system. She further announced that the Comprehensive Annual
Financial Report, also known as the CAFR, is available on the City's website for those who are
interested. The Management Discussion and Analysis in the beginning of the document is
particularly interesting and provides a very good outline of the audited numbers. Mayor Reardon
discussed her attendance at the Pony League Black Hawks 9U tournament where she had the
pleasure of throwing out the first ball. She was not only impressed by the skill of the team but it
was apparent that the kids and the coaches enjoy being together. Mayor Reardon stated that 2013
is going to be an interesting year and she again thanked everyone for giving up their time to come
to the meeting.

ADJOURNMENT

Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting to Monday, January 21, 2013, at 5:00 p.m.
